output.proposal: HB No. 10697 seeks to establish the National Coordinating Council for Education (NCCE) under the Office of the President as a permanent, high-level inter-agency body to direct, coordinate and monitor education and workforce development reforms across the Executive Branch. It aims to address the learning crisis and keep education reforms and priorities consistent across administrations.
output.alignment: As a government organization measure, the review should examine how the NCCE fits with existing education agencies and inter-agency mechanisms, including those established under Administrative Order No. 36, s. 2025, cited in Section 5 (Powers and Functions), and whether the convergence arrangement in Section 9 (Rationalization and Convergence of Inter-Agency Bodies) and the new Secretariat under Section 8 (The Council Secretariat) are consistent with the streamlining and reduction of overlapping functions under the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231). The measure aligns with the Human Capital Development priority area of the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework, particularly its focus on equitable access to quality education. It is not identified in the LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda.
legislative_history: HB No. 10697 was filed in the House of Representatives on August 11, 2026 by Representative Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez; it is pending at the filing stage, and later stages are not reflected in available records.
HB No. 11217 of the 20th Congress carries the same title and near-identical provisions.
Other 20th Congress measures proposing a National Coordinating Council for Education with different designs include HB No. 9132, HB No. 9573, HB No. 10761 and HB No. 11275.

In the 18th Congress, HB No. 2746 and HB No. 4925 (National Education Coordinating Council) and HB No. 7807 and HB No. 8022 (National Education Council) addressed a similar subject; only their titles were reviewed, and all were pending in committee.
No Senate counterpart, committee report or substitute bill was identified.

output.salient_features:
HB No. 10697 seeks to establish the National Coordinating Council for Education (NCCE) as a high-level inter-agency body under the Office of the President. Its salient features are as follows:
a. Section 3 (Creation of the National Coordinating Council for Education) provides that the NCCE is created under, and supervised by, the Office of the President as the primary mechanism for directing, coordinating and monitoring education and workforce development reforms, and for aligning agency policies, plans, programs and budgets with the National Education and Workforce Development Plan.
b. Section 4 (Composition of the Council) provides that the President chairs the Council, may designate a Cabinet Secretary as Vice Chairperson, and that the heads of DepEd, CHED, TESDA, DOST, DOLE, DBM and DEPDev serve as members.
c. Section 5 (Powers and Functions) provides that the Council shall harmonize education policies and programs, implement and update the National Education and Workforce Development Plan, converge with existing inter-agency mechanisms, monitor priority reforms including those identified by EDCOM II, develop a human resource plan for the education sector, and review and endorse major education sector budget proposals before submission to DBM, among others.
d. Section 6 (Technical Working Groups) provides that the Council may create Technical Working Groups of senior officials of at least Assistant Secretary or Director IV level, and may invite other agencies, industry and educational associations and sectoral representatives.
e. Section 7 (Convergence and Accountability) provides that member agencies shall assist the Council, share data, remain accountable for aligned programs, and report under a results-based monitoring and evaluation framework.
f. Section 8 (The Council Secretariat) provides for a Secretariat as the Council's technical and program management arm, headed by an Executive Director with the rank of Undersecretary appointed by the President, staffed by permanent personnel and augmented by seconded personnel, technical experts and contracted specialists.
g. Section 9 (Rationalization and Convergence of Inter-Agency Bodies) provides that existing inter-agency bodies with substantially similar mandates or memberships shall, to the extent practicable, coordinate through the Council, whose meetings are deemed compliance with those bodies' meeting requirements.
h. Section 10 (Appropriations) provides that initial funding shall be charged against the current appropriations of the Office of the President, and that subsequent funding shall be included in the Office of the President's budget proposal in the annual General Appropriations Act.
output.related_measures_policy: HB No. 10697 may be considered alongside HB No. 11217, which is near-identical, and HB Nos. 9132, 9573, 10761 and 11275, which propose the same council with differing membership, functions and funding arrangements; these may be considered for consolidation. The measure aligns with the Human Capital Development priority of the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework. The review should assess whether a new statutory council and a Secretariat headed by an Undersecretary-rank official are warranted given existing education coordinating bodies, such as the Literacy Coordinating Council under RA No. 7165 as amended by RA No. 10122, and the mechanisms under Administrative Order No. 36, s. 2025, and whether Section 9 (Rationalization and Convergence of Inter-Agency Bodies) achieves the streamlining intended by RA No. 12231. The review should also assess the budget review role of the Council under Section 5 (Powers and Functions) in relation to the existing budget preparation process.
